lens.subject: Does every reaction now go through one bundle per run?
lens.message:
The memory you saved settles where reaction delivery belongs. You put it this way: "we route every reaction through one bundle per run per person, not one message per skill — a person should get one thing to read, not four". The bundle closes when the run closes, and a skill that misses the close waits for the next run rather than sending on its own. The per-skill alternative with client-side collapsing was considered and rejected.

[The reaction delivery doc](docs/reaction-delivery.md) says the opposite in its opening: "Each reaction skill sends its own message to the person as soon as it finishes" and "Readers collapse duplicates on their side." That is the rejected alternative, written as the current rule. After the change, the opening would say every reaction routes through one bundle per run per person, that the bundle closes when the run closes, and that a late skill waits for the next run. Collapsing would no longer be the reader's job.

Is that the right way to read what you ruled: one bundle per run per person, with late skills waiting for the next run? If I have it wrong, tell me how.

This is the only document in the repo that describes reaction delivery, so nothing else moves.

After the change, this opening would say every reaction routes through one bundle per run per person, the bundle closes when the run closes, and a skill that misses the close waits for the next run. Collapsing would no longer be the reader's job.
